nodes.title: the Glimzam signature
nodes.statement: The Glimzam system concerns objects called mornglims. There are exactly 4 of them: oviazt, kapon, nyrrast, xilwren. One operation is written |. One relation is written <~, read as "dominates".

nodes.title: the Glimzam combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x | y for every pair of mornglims is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the <~ relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all mornglims x and y, x | y is again a mornglim.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all mornglims x, y, z: (x | y) | z = x | (y | z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all mornglims x and y: x | y = y | x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a mornglim oviazt with oviazt | x = x | oviazt = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: For every mornglim x: x | x = x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a mornglim xilwren with xilwren | x = x | xilwren = xilwren for every x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every mornglim x: x <~ x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all mornglims x and y: if x <~ y and y <~ x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all mornglims x, y, z: if x <~ y and y <~ z then x <~ z.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all mornglims x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z | x) <~ (z | y) and (x | z) <~ (y | z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some mornglim x admits no mornglim y for which x | y and y | x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kapon, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all mornglims x, y, z: if x | y = x | z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kapon, y = oviazt, z = kapon, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all mornglims x and y, at least one of x <~ y and y <~ x holds.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kapon, y = nyrrast, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: iskzam mornglims
nodes.statement: A mornglim x is called iskzam when x | x = x.

nodes.title: mornglims that zelvex
nodes.statement: Two mornglims x and y are said to zelvex when x | y = y | x.

nodes.title: tezdri collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of mornglims is tezdri when x | y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the nakhurn of a mornglim
nodes.statement: The nakhurn of a mornglim x is the collection of mornglims y for which x <~ y holds.

nodes.title: the vexbra
nodes.statement: The mornglim oviazt is called the vexbra of the system. It is the unique mornglim that leaves every mornglim unchanged under |.

nodes.title: the falespa
nodes.statement: The falespa of the system is the collection of mornglims that zelvex with every mornglim.

nodes.title: the xilka
nodes.statement: The xilka is the collection of all iskzam mornglims.

nodes.title: the clobra of a mornglim
nodes.statement: The clobra of a mornglim x, written [x], is the smallest tezdri collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a duthvor
nodes.statement: A mornglim f is a duthvor when f <~ y holds for every mornglim y, that is, when the nakhurn of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: rastshen mornglims
nodes.statement: A mornglim x is rastshen when x | x equals the vexbra.

nodes.title: the nakdri of a mornglim
nodes.statement: The nakdri of a mornglim x is the number of mornglims in its clobra [x].

nodes.title: the grixvor
nodes.statement: The grixvor of the system is the collection of mornglims whose nakdri is largest.

nodes.title: dripon pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct mornglims x and y form a dripon pair when x <~ y and y <~ x both hold, that is, when each lies in the nakhurn of the other.

nodes.title: the vexbra is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one mornglim e with e | x = x | e = x for every mornglim x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every mornglim unchanged.
Then e | f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e | f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the vexbra lies in the falespa
nodes.statement: The vexbra zelvexs with every mornglim.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the vexbra and x any mornglim.
Then e | x = x and x | e = x.
So e | x = x | e, which is what it means to zelvex.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the falespa.

nodes.title: the falespa is tezdri
nodes.statement: If x and y both zelvex with every mornglim, then so does x | y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the falespa and let z be any mornglim.
Then (x | y) | z = x | (y | z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each zelvexs with everything.
So x | y zelvexs with z, and the falespa is tezdri.

nodes.title: the clobra of a mornglim is tezdri
nodes.statement: For every mornglim x, the collection [x] is tezdri.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under |.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the clobra is contained in every tezdri collection
nodes.statement: If S is tezdri and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a mornglim is iskzam exactly when its nakdri is one
nodes.statement: x | x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x | x = x then {x} is already closed under |.
So [x] = {x} and the nakdri is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x | x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the nakdri divides the number of mornglims
nodes.statement: For every mornglim x, the nakdri of x divides 4.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a tezdri collection.
Its size is the nakdri of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 4.

nodes.title: the clobra of a falespa mornglim stays in the falespa
nodes.statement: If x lies in the falespa then every mornglim of [x] lies in the falespa.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The falespa is tezdri.
[x] is the smallest tezdri collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the falespa is one.

nodes.title: the xilka is tezdri
nodes.statement: If x and y are both iskzam then so is x | y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be iskzam.
The claim asks whether (x | y) | (x | y) returns x | y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: nakhurns are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the nakhurn of x, then the nakhurn of y is contained in the nakhurn of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <~ y and let z satisfy y <~ z.
Transitivity gives x <~ z.
So every member of the nakhurn of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one duthvor
nodes.statement: No two distinct mornglims can both be duthvors.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f <~ h, since h is any object, and h <~ f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x <~ y then (x | z) <~ (y | z) for every mornglim z.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the nakhurn of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: no dripon pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct mornglims lie in each other's nakhurn.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every mornglim lies in the falespa
nodes.statement: Every pair of mornglims zelvexs.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The falespa is defined by zelvexing with everything.
The claim is that x | y = y | x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: every mornglim is iskzam
nodes.statement: x | x = x for every mornglim x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Being iskzam is the condition x | x = x.
The claim is that the xilka is the whole system.
Only the diagonal of the table is involved.

nodes.title: where some mornglim reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a mornglim whose clobra is the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 1, size = 4, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x <~ y then y <~ x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = oviazt, y = kapon, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the vexbra swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e | x equals the vexbra for every mornglim x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = oviazt, x = kapon, value = kapon, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.
